fixes.title: Readiness panel reported a green "Profile devices — every device is connected" over an empty profile with nothing connected
fixes.summary: Confirmed the verifier's location correction: readiness_panel.dart only renders what it is handed; the vacuous pass was _buildProfileDevices in packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/models/readiness/readiness_models.dart, which returned ReadinessLevel.ready whenever offlineProfileDevices was empty. An EMPTY profile produces an empty offline list, so 'Every device assigned in the active profile is connected.' was true over an empty set. The input the rule needed did not exist, so I added assignedProfileDeviceSlotsProvider (the assignment SET, next to the existing offline-subset provider) and three required parameters on buildReadinessReport: hasActiveProfile, assignedProfileDeviceCount and otherAssignedProfileDeviceCount. Required, not defaulted, so a future caller cannot silently reintroduce the vacuous pass. Three empty-set shapes now get honest sentences: no active profile -> 'No equipment profile is active, so there are no device assignments to check.' (ready, since criticalDevices already blocks on the missing profile); zero assignments -> CAUTION 'No devices are assigned to this profile, so nothing connects automatically.' with a Fix route to /equipment; camera+mount-only -> ready but 'This profile assigns no accessories beyond the camera and mount'. The all-connected sentence was also rescoped to 'Every accessory ... (camera and mount are covered above)' because camera/mount are filtered out of this row's input, so the old wording could claim connectivity for a disconnected camera.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_core/test/providers/readiness_provider_test.dart — 3 new tests: 'profile with zero assigned devices -> profileDevices caution, not a vacuous all-connected pass' (camera+mount disconnected, empty assignment set), 'camera/mount-only profile -> profileDevices ready without claiming every device is connected', 'no active profile -> profileDevices makes no assignment claim'. Provider-level on purpose so the test covers the wiring, not just the pure rule.
fixes.revert_check: Severed the production wiring in readiness_provider.dart: replaced `assignedProfileDeviceCount: assignedProfileSlots.length, otherAssignedProfileDeviceCount: otherAssignedProfileSlots.length` with the literals `4` / `2`. flutter test test/providers/readiness_provider_test.dart -> +18 -2 (zero-assigned and camera/mount-only tests failed). Restored -> 20/20 pass; full core set (readiness models + provider + next_use_prompt + weather contract + 2 weather providers) 74/74 pass.
fixes.caveats: readiness_models.dart / readiness_provider.dart / profile_connection_status_provider.dart are in skotiq_core, outside this agent's widgets/** ownership. The verifier's location_wrong note is explicit that the cited widget file cannot hold the fix, so the change was made where the text and level are actually decided. buildReadinessReport's new parameters are required, which forced the three existing test call sites to be updated.

fixes.title: Dismissing a blocking readiness item hid it while the summary kept counting it
fixes.summary: Two halves, matching the verifier's correction. (1) packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/readiness/readiness_panel.dart: blocked rows are no longer dismissable — the ✕ is not rendered on a blocked row, and the dismissal filter refuses to hide a blocked item even if its id is already in the session set. A hard blocker is by definition the thing the operator cannot defer, and hiding it is what made the count and the list disagree. Caution rows keep the ✕, which is what it was added for (plate solver, dark library). (2) packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/equipment/widgets/equipment_readiness_panel.dart:_subtitle: the header now subtracts the dismissed caution rows from the count it quotes and appends ' (N dismissed)', so the number equals the rows on screen. The same treatment was applied to ReadinessPanel's own _summaryDetail banner (the dialog path) so the invariant holds wherever the panel is hosted, rather than being patched only on the surface the audit happened to hit.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/widgets/readiness/readiness_dismissal_count_test.dart — 3 tests: a blocking row offers no ✕ (while the caution row still does); a blocker whose id is already in the dismissed set is still listed and the header still reads '2 items are blocking first light.' with two blocking rows visible; dismissing a caution row moves the header from '2 items to review before imaging.' to '1 item to review before imaging (1 dismissed).'
fixes.revert_check: Reverted both call sites: readiness_panel.dart's filter back to `baseItems.where((i) => !dismissed.contains(i.id)).toList()` and `onDismiss: dismissible` (dropping the level guard), plus equipment_readiness_panel.dart's `outstanding` back to blocked+caution with no hiddenCaution subtraction and dismissedNote blanked. flutter test -> 0 passed, 3 failed. Restored -> 3/3 pass, and the pre-existing equipment_readiness_panel_test.dart + equipment_status_rail_idle_test.dart stay green.
fixes.caveats: equipment_readiness_panel.dart is under screens/, outside widgets/**; the verifier identified it as the file holding the lying count string, and readiness_panel.dart alone is only half the fix. Unrelated PRE-EXISTING failure noted: the 3 equipment golden captures in test/screens/equipment/captures_landscape_test.dart fail with 21.6/24.8/26.8% pixel diffs — byte-identical diffs reproduce with both readiness files checked out to HEAD, so they are not caused by this change (Linux-vs-Windows golden debt).

fixes.title: 'Disconnect All' stayed enabled and silently no-opped when nothing was connected
fixes.summary: packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/equipment_status_indicator.dart:_buildDropdownItems now passes `enabled: canDisconnect` on the Disconnect All PopupMenuItem and greys its icon + label (the item sets an explicit textPrimary colour, so PopupMenuItem's own disabled styling would not have shown). The enablement predicate reads the SAME target list the sweep walks — `equipmentDisconnectTargets(ref).any((t) => !equipmentDisconnectShouldSkip(t.connectionState))` — not the chip's `counts`. That distinction is the whole point: the chip only tallies the six profile-assignable slots, while runEquipmentDisconnectAll also covers dome, weather station, safety monitor, switch and cover calibrator, so gating on `counts.totalConnected` would have inverted the defect by grey-ing out a button that still had a connected dome to disconnect.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/widgets/equipment_status_indicator_test.dart — 3 new tests reading PopupMenuItem.enabled for value 'disconnect': disabled with nothing connected; enabled with a camera connected; and enabled with only a DOME connected (the chip reads '0 connected' in that frame) — the anti-inversion case.
fixes.revert_check: Deleted the literal line `enabled: canDisconnect,` from the PopupMenuItem. flutter test test/widgets/equipment_status_indicator_test.dart -> +6 -1, 'Disconnect All is disabled when nothing is connected' failed; the two enabled-side tests stayed green, so the test pins the gate rather than the button's existence. Restored -> 7/7 pass.

fixes.title: Guiding-control buttons were invisible to assistive tech (role 'panel', never DISABLED)
fixes.summary: Confirmed the verifier's method correction — the shared builder is _buildControlButton at guide_controls_panel.dart:765, not '_actionButton'. It returned a bare Material > InkWell > ConstrainedBox > AnimatedContainer > Row(Icon, Text) with no Semantics, and when disabled it passed onTap: null so the InkWell published no tap semantics either; the only node reaching AT-SPI was the unnamed generic container the audit saw as 'panel: Start'. Wrapped the whole control in Semantics(container: true, button: true, enabled: !isDisabled, label: label, onTap: …, excludeSemantics: true). excludeSemantics keeps the inner Text from publishing a second, unactionable label node; the tap action is republished on the Semantics node so screen-reader activation is not lost along with it. This covers all six controls the audit named (Start, Pause, Loop Exposures, Auto Select, Deselect, Dither Now) plus Stop/Resume, because they all route through the one builder.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/widgets/phd2/guide_controls_panel_semantics_test.dart — 3 tests under a live SemanticsHandle: PHD2 disconnected -> Start is isSemantics(label:'Start', isButton:true, hasEnabledState:true, isEnabled:false); PHD2 connected -> isEnabled:true with hasTapAction:true; and the semantics tap action actually reaches the callback (guards against excludeSemantics silently costing activation).
fixes.revert_check: Neutralised the wrapper's published contract at the call site — deleted `button: true`, `enabled: !isDisabled` and `label: label` from the Semantics node, leaving the widget tree byte-identical otherwise (so this is an assertion failure, not a compile error). flutter test -> all 3 semantics tests failed; the 11 pre-existing guide_controls_panel_test.dart behaviour tests stayed green. Restored -> 28/28 pass across the phd2 + slew suites.

fixes.title: Weather status card rendered an epoch-zero timestamp as 'Updated 20667 days ago' before the first fetch
fixes.summary: The verifier was right that a fixer sent only to the card finds a null-guard that already exists. Root cause was weather_providers.dart:582 `lastUpdate: lastFetchedAt ?? DateTime.fromMillisecondsSinceEpoch(0)` against a NON-NULLABLE WeatherStatus.lastUpdate, so the card's `if (widget.lastUpdate != null)` could never be false. Made WeatherStatus.lastUpdate nullable (freezed source + regenerated weather_status.freezed.dart / .g.dart via a build-filtered build_runner run) and dropped the sentinel from the provider, so 'no fetch has landed' is now representable. In the card the footer no longer disappears silently: it renders 'Waiting for weather data' when lastUpdate is null and the age string only once there is a real fetch time to age from. No arbitrary staleness threshold was added — that would just relocate the sentinel into a magic constant.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/widgets/weather/weather_status_card_last_update_test.dart — null lastUpdate renders 'Waiting for weather data' and never any 'days ago'/'Updated' text; a real timestamp renders 'Updated 3 min ago'. Plus packages/skotiq_core/test/providers/weather_status_contract_test.dart, whose existing assertion `expect(status.lastUpdate, DateTime.fromMillisecondsSinceEpoch(0))` had LOCKED THE BUG IN and now asserts isNull.
fixes.revert_check: Reverted both call sites: weather_providers.dart back to `lastFetchedAt ?? DateTime.fromMillisecondsSinceEpoch(0)` and the card back to `if (widget.lastUpdate != null) Text('Updated …')`. flutter test -> the card test 'no fetch yet -> says it is waiting' failed. Restored -> 5/5 weather widget tests and 74/74 core tests pass.
fixes.caveats: The 3 weather golden captures in test/screens/weather/captures_landscape_test.dart fail (45-48% pixel diff) — PRE-EXISTING and unrelated: I verified identical diffs with my card change reverted to HEAD, and those tests hit the live mesonet WMS endpoint (400s in the log). Model + provider changes are in skotiq_core, outside widgets/**; the verifier's correction says the fix belongs there.

fixes.title: The Slew split-button was invisible to assistive tech — no node at all
fixes.summary: PopupMenuButton's child path is Semantics(expanded:…) > Tooltip('Show menu') > InkWell — it publishes a tap action and an expanded flag but no name and no button role, and the only labelled descendant here is deliberately inside ExcludeSemantics (removing that would produce a second, unactionable 'Slew' node from SkotiqButton's own Semantics). Wrapped the PopupMenuButton in Semantics(button: true, enabled: enabled, label: visibleLabel, hint: 'Opens slew options'); the annotations merge into the InkWell's existing node, so the result is one node with name + role + enabled state + tap action rather than a parent/child pair. The label tracks the RENDERED text ('Slew', or the caller's label, or 'Working...' while in flight) so voice control can target it by what the user reads; the menu-opening nature is carried by the hint instead of by mangling the name.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/widgets/slew_dropdown_button_test.dart — 2 new tests under a live SemanticsHandle: mount connected -> isSemantics(label:'Slew', isButton:true, hasEnabledState:true, isEnabled:true, hasTapAction:true); mount disconnected -> the same node with isEnabled:false (rather than vanishing).
fixes.revert_check: Neutralised the wrapper at the call site — deleted `button: true`, `enabled: enabled`, `label: visibleLabel` and `hint:` from the Semantics node. flutter test -> both new tests failed ('publishes a named, enabled button node', 'publishes the disabled state when the mount is down') while the 6 pre-existing horizon-gate / single-flight tests stayed green. Restored -> 28/28 pass.
fixes.caveats: The verifier's recorded trap holds: with the coordinate fields EMPTY, mount_tab.dart renders a plain disabled SkotiqButton instead of this dropdown, so a live re-check must fill in RA/Dec first.

fixes.title: Dashboard Glance-mode toggle reported itself as DISABLED to assistive tech while working normally
fixes.summary: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/dashboard/widgets/glance_mode_toggle.dart:60-63 set Semantics(button: true, toggled: enabled, label: 'Glance mode') with no `enabled:`, so the node published CHECKABLE but never ENABLED/SENSITIVE — the tree read '[off,DISABLED]' and '[ON,DISABLED]' after a click. Added `enabled: !_saving`, which is the real state: the only thing that disables the tap is an in-flight settings write.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/dashboard/widgets/glance_mode_toggle_test.dart — 'a working toggle announces itself as enabled' asserts isSemantics(label:'Glance mode', isButton:true, hasEnabledState:true, isEnabled:true, hasToggledState:true, isToggled:false) under a live SemanticsHandle.
fixes.revert_check: Deleted the literal line `enabled: !_saving,` from the Semantics node. flutter test -> 'a working toggle announces itself as enabled' failed while the pre-existing failed-persistence test stayed green. Restored -> 2/2 pass.
fixes.caveats: glance_mode_toggle.dart is under screens/dashboard/, outside widgets/**; the finding was filed against its TouchTargetFloor wrapper (widgets/touch_target_floor.dart) and the verifier confirmed the toggle file as the correct location.

fixes.title: Four widgets exported from the app barrel with zero call sites — dead UI shipping in the binary
fixes.summary: Split by what each one actually was. DELETED (superseded, zero references anywhere including tests): widgets/object_info_panel.dart (299 lines, superseded by the planetarium's object_details_panel) and widgets/tour_selection_sheet.dart (616 lines, whose own doc asserted 'Used from Settings and contextual prompts' while Settings > Help & Tutorials builds a richer inline Tutorial Tours section with per-category progress/resume/restart). DELETED with its coverage MOVED rather than dropped: widgets/sequence_controls.dart (179 lines) had exactly one reference — test/widgets/run_controls_paused_skip_test.dart, a canSkip-while-paused regression test pinned to a surface that no screen mounts. The mobile playback bar that actually ships is screens/sequencer/widgets/mobile_playback_bar.dart, so that test case was retargeted to MobilePlaybackBar (which routes skip through executionState.canSkip), turning a test of nothing into a test of the real surface. All three barrel exports removed from lib/skotiq_app.dart, and the two stale `SequenceControls` references in mobile_sequence_overlay.dart's doc corrected to MobilePlaybackBar. WIRED rather than deleted: VariablePickerField/VariablePickerButton is a correct, tested mirror of the Rust interpolation catalog, and the verifier's user-facing half was a real capability gap — so VariablePickerButton is now the suffixIcon of the live-stacking Watermark template field (screens/sequencer/widgets/live_stacking_properties.dart), the one field in the app whose value is interpolated at render time and whose helper text previously listed ${target} / ${integration.hms} / ${frames} / ${stack.method} for the operator to type from memory. Also corrected one factual error in the claim: variable_picker.dart is NOT barrel-exported (three of the four were, the fourth was unexported).
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/widgets/sequence/variable_picker_wiring_test.dart — the watermark field renders exactly one VariablePickerButton, it is bound to the WATERMARK controller (asserted via the ancestor TextField's controller text, not just presence), and opening it lists 'integration.hms'. Plus the retargeted 'the mobile playback bar dispatches a skip while PAUSED' in run_controls_paused_skip_test.dart.
fixes.revert_check: Deleted the `suffixIcon: VariablePickerButton(...)` block from live_stacking_properties.dart. flutter test test/widgets/sequence/variable_picker_wiring_test.dart -> failed. Restored -> pass. The deletion half has no behaviour to revert; it is verified by `dart analyze lib test` reporting zero errors across skotiq_app with the three files and their barrel exports gone, and by the retargeted test compiling only against MobilePlaybackBar.
fixes.caveats: live_stacking_properties.dart is under screens/sequencer/, outside widgets/**; it was the only field in the app that the picker was written for. The four other watermark-ish text inputs in Settings > Sequencer go through the shared settingsTrailingTextInput -> SettingsTextInput -> SkotiqTextField(suffix:) chain, which renders its suffix only when the field is focused/non-empty; threading a proper always-visible affordance through that shared helper is a cross-package design-system change I judged out of proportion to a P4 and did NOT attempt.

incident.what: At 22:45:29 a concurrent agent ran `git stash` on the shared worktree, reverting all 460 tracked files of uncommitted campaign work (29k insertions) to HEAD — including every source edit in this batch. New untracked test files survived; edits to tracked test files did not. At ~22:47 the same or another agent applied the stash back and all of this batch's work returned intact (verified file-by-file, then re-ran every test in this report green).
incident.residual_risk: stash@{0} STILL EXISTS after the apply. If anyone pops or applies it again it will now conflict with the restored tree. Someone should verify the tree is correct and then `git stash drop stash@{0}`.
incident.verification_after_recovery: skotiq_app: 66 tests green across widgets/readiness, equipment_status_indicator, widgets/phd2, slew_dropdown_button, widgets/weather, glance_mode_toggle, widgets/sequence, run_controls_paused_skip, variable_picker, equipment_status_rail_idle. skotiq_core: 74 green across readiness models/provider, next_use_prompt, weather status contract, weather abstention/unreachable. dart analyze clean (zero errors/warnings in every file this batch touched) and dart format --set-exit-if-changed clean on all 27.
